steps.text: Whenever SSI0 sends a frame, PA3 (the OLED chip select) is not the SSI0 frame signal and is not driven low.
The LDO voltage is raised to 2.75V before enabling the PLL to address the Rev A2 silicon errata
The system clock is 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal through the PLL whenever the UART or SSI is in use, and the chip never runs from a disabled or misconfigured clock on the way there.
At least 3 system clock cycles must pass after a peripheral's clock is enabled before the peripheral is accessed.
Card identification, including the power-up clocks before CMD0, runs between 100 kHz and 400 kHz, with the prescaler's lowest bit ignored as the hardware does.
SSI0's clock settings (SSICR0 and SSICPSR) are written only while the port is disabled.

Reading and writing work on version 1, standard and high-capacity cards, with the right card type reported and no stray writes. Card start-up follows the SD SPI rules, UART and SSI pins and clocks are set up before use, the UART runs at 115200 baud 8N1 within 2 %, and SPI data runs at 10-25 MHz.
When a different card is inserted and initialised again, identification runs at 100-400 kHz again and the new card reads correctly with its own addressing.
A block number past the end of the card gets an error on every card type, including numbers that would overflow a 32-bit byte address, and the low block such a number would wrap to is left unchanged.
On a 16 GB high-capacity card, reads and writes work at block numbers with eight digits.
